You take off your wet boots and sleep. The storm blows itself thin around the shutters, and Kit snores across the room like a woman felling a small tree. It is a poor sleep and a good one, and you wake to a rain-washed sky going amber at the window.

Pell comes at dusk, as promised, with his halberd left downstairs and a folded sheet in his fist. He says the clerk never touched it and goes away again. You read it by the lamp.

It is a map in Corvin's plain hand, with none of his usual flourishes. It shows the lower Marrow road, the east bank, and a crossing marked Sallow Cross, about a day and a half upriver of Saltmarsh. Beside a small square he has written: *Reedlight Shrine. Keeper: Goody Nan Berrow. About fifteen years back. The child wore a blue wool coat with a wren stitched on the collar.* Under that, a line you read twice: *Aldous does not know this place. I have never told a soul.* He has signed it with his small drawn lantern.

You set it beside Elowen's letter and the strip from the lamp-staff. Neither names a place, so there is nothing to check it against, but one thing sits badly. Brann said Elowen left you "among people who will love her". Corvin says a woman who took coin and asked nothing. Both can be true, because a mother can believe a thing and be wrong. The coat with the wren is a detail he could have invented, but he never once mentioned a coat in all your years on the road.

Over supper, bread and eel pie from Bess Harl, Kit listens to all of it and chews. "Two jobs," she says at last. "The reliquary on the spit, and Brann with it. And this Sallow Cross." She nods at the map. "Or Thornhallow, to ask about the name. I'd not leave the old man out there long, with the grey sail about."

Your long rest can't finish until about four in the morning. The Heron's Tithe has not been seen in the harbour since the squall. Dame Crowe's assize is at the end of the month, and Corvin must reach Marrowford alive. What does Wren do?

You sleep like a stone. When you wake the fire has burned low, the rain has thinned to a drip, and the shutters have stopped rattling. Kit is already up, sharpening her sword by the hearth. It's past six, and the light in the window is going grey. Pell knocks soon after, damp to the knees. He hands you a folded sheet and doesn't wait to be thanked.

Corvin's map is neat, in the careful hand he used for his best forgeries. It shows the lower Marrow, a reed-bed crossing marked REEDMOOR, and a small lantern-mark beside a building labelled *the Wayhouse*, a day's ride upriver from Saltmarsh. Beneath it he has written: *Keeper: Nan Orchard, a widow then, red-handed, took boarders' coin. Sixteen winters back. Elowen left you in her care in the autumn and was not seen there again. Burn this if you think me a liar, and ride there if you think me a fool.* He has signed it with the little drawn lantern.

You lay it beside Elowen's letter and the strip from the staff, and you can't make them talk. Your Investigation roll is a natural 1 with disadvantage, a total of 3. You read the same lines three times without finding a thing that matches or contradicts. Reedmoor isn't in the letter, but the letter is short and says little about places. Maybe it fits, maybe it doesn't. You can't tell from the page, and you'd have to go and look.

Over stew, Kit listens to you lay it all out and gives her verdict in her usual way. "Reedmoor's a day's ride. The reliquary's on the spit. Hale's at Thornhallow. Crowe's assize is at month's end." She chews. "Pick one first."

Outside, the storm has blown itself out, and across the estuary the Gullspit light is a steady white star. You've no spell slots, one Bardic Inspiration, and exhaustion 1 until the long rest finishes before dawn. What does Wren do?

Names the shrine-house as the Reed-Lamp, a lantern-sign roadside house at Sallow Reach on the lower Marrow, about a day and a half by road east of Saltmarsh along the estuary shore, kept sixteen years ago by Goodwife Tamsin Aske, who took coin to keep a child. He wrote she may be dead or moved. Wren's Investigation (4) could not tell whether the map is honest or doctored. The Reed-Lamp is not named in Elowen's letter or strip.

You sleep the afternoon away by the fire. The storm blows itself thin against the shutters. Kit snores like a patient saw. You wake stiff and dry, with the light going grey in the window.

Pell arrives a little after six, rain on his shoulders, and hands you a folded sheet without a word. Then he goes back down to the taproom, where Bess Harl is putting out bowls of stew.

It is Corvin's hand, small and neat, with no flourish. The map is a rough sketch of the estuary shore running east from Saltmarsh. A day and a half along it, where a creek meets the lower Marrow, he has drawn a small lantern and a name: the Reed-Lamp, at Sallow Reach. Below it he has written: "Goodwife Tamsin Aske kept it sixteen years ago. She took coin, asked nothing, and had a cough. She may be dead. She may have moved. I have not been back." It is unsigned, except for a tiny lantern.

You look it over by the lamp. Elowen's letter and the strip of paper name no place that matches, so there is nothing to check it against. You turn the page over and hold it to the light, and your Investigation is a 4 (disadvantage again). You can't tell whether the ink, the hurry or the lines hide anything. It could be honest. It could also be exactly what he would draw to send you somewhere convenient to him.

Over supper Kit chews, listens and says only, "East. Day and a half. Same road he might want us on." Then she adds, "Or Marrowford first. Assize at month's end, the reliquary on the spit, the rider to Lord Edric." She shrugs. "Your call."

It is about a quarter past six on Day 10. Your long rest can't finish before about four in the morning, you have no slots, and the lamp still burns on the spit. What does Wren decide?

entries.text: notebook: updated Corvin Tallowmere

You sleep through the afternoon with the fire ticking and the storm easing against the shutters. Kit snores like a patient saw. It isn't a long rest, since that can't finish before the small hours, but you wake with a clearer head. Exhaustion 1 still sits on you, and your slots are still empty.

Pell knocks at dusk, rain on his cloak. He hands over a folded sheet and says only, "Written at the cot, in his own hand. I watched." Then he goes.

You read it by the lamp. It's a plain map, drawn without flourish. A willow-lined bend of the lower Marrow, half a day's ride upriver of Saltmarsh. A standing stone with a lantern cut into it. A low wayhouse beside it, labelled *Sallow Reach Shrine*. Beneath it is a line: *Goodwife Hesper Wyle. Ask her for the cradle-song.* Below that, the small drawn lantern he signs with.

You go through Elowen's letter and the strip from the staff. The shrine isn't named in either. The letter does say you'd be "safe among people who will love her", and Brann remembers her saying "far from the man who sells lanterns". That fits a quiet wayhouse and doesn't contradict anything, but it proves nothing either. It's the kind of detail Corvin would draw if it were true, and also the kind he'd draw if it weren't. A half-day upriver is also a handy place to lure a girl who has just left a well-guarded town. Pell, hovering in the doorway, would be the first to say so.

Supper comes up from Bess Harl: bread, eel pie and a jug of thin cider. Kit sits up, rubs her face and starts eating without comment. Outside the lamp on the spit still burns, a white thread through the thinning rain.

Open before you: Sallow Reach, a day's ride there and back. The reliquary waiting with Brann on the spit. Dame Crowe's assize at month's end, and Corvin to be brought to it. Lord Edric's answer about "Aldous", due in two or three days. Your long rest can't finish until about four tomorrow morning.

Kit looks at you over her bread. "Well?"

What does Wren decide?
